_readme: THE GOLDEN-PATH LEG REGISTER — [pipeline N-6] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/06-app-build.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
N-6 names a SIX-LEG golden path — anonymous -> sign in -> purchase (sandbox) -> entitlement flips
-> feature unlocks -> account delete purges — and asks for exactly one integration E2E on web that
covers it, wired into a named workflow.
THE DEFECT THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. Measured 2026-07-29 and re-measured 2026-08-02: the only
implementation of that path in the tree, apps/subscriptiontracker/integration_test/app_test.dart, declares TWO
tests and proves TWO of the six legs. There is no purchase, no entitlement flip, no feature unlock
and no account delete in it. So a green, non-skipped, fresh nightly still does not mean what N-6
says it means — and until this register existed, nothing anywhere wrote that number down. A
criterion whose right-hand side is undefined cannot reject anything.
🔄 THREE OF SIX SINCE 2026-08-08. `account-delete-purges` moved to `asserted`: the suite now
declares THREE tests and the third walks the erasure end to end against the deployed API. The two
sentences above are left as written because they are a dated measurement, not a status line — the
count that is checked is the one assert-e2e-legs.mjs computes on every run, and a prose number
edited by hand is the second copy that drifts. The three legs still blocked are the money rail's,
and they share one live blocker.
🔴 THE RULE THAT MAKES THIS FILE MEAN ANYTHING: A LEG IS 'asserted' ONLY IF THE SUITE PROVES IT.
Every `asserted` leg carries `anchors` — expressions that must appear in the E2E's
COMMENT-STRIPPED source. tooling/ci/assert-e2e-legs.mjs resolves each one; a leg that claims to be
asserted and whose anchors no longer resolve fails the build. That is the equality N-6 asks for:
the number of legs the record claims equals the number the suite actually proves.
Comment-stripping is not a formality here. app_test.dart's own header narrates the six-night
outage and contains the string `tap('Skip')` inside a comment, so a raw-text scan would resolve
the onboarding anchor against the PROSE DESCRIBING THE BUG rather than against any test.
🔴 A BLOCKED LEG'S EXCUSE IS ITSELF CHECKED. Every `blocked` leg names a `blockedBy` that
assert-e2e-legs.mjs re-evaluates against the real tree on every run (the BLOCKERS_STILL_REAL
pattern from assert-screen-set.mjs). If the blocker has shipped, the build FAILS — so 'blocked by
the money rail' cannot outlive the money rail, and the day apps/subscriptiontracker starts selling something the
three legs below stop being excusable in the same run. Blocked legs also PRINT on every run; a gap
that is silent is a gap nobody closes.
⚠️ WEB ONLY, BY POLICY, AND DATED. The cut was taken 2026-07-29. Apple 3.1.1 and Play's billing
policy require IAP for digital goods, so a Paddle web checkout cannot be the unlock path on iOS or
Android AT ALL — the purchase->unlock leg is not merely unimplemented off web, it is structurally
invalid there, and the IAP rail is routed to [5]/[10]. The other four platforms' absence is a COST
choice and not a tooling limit: `flutter test integration_test/` is documented for Android, iOS,
Windows, macOS and Linux (Linux needs xvfb-run), and the cheapest widening is Linux desktop on the
ubuntu runner already paid for. MASTER_PLAN.md:163 (DoD §4-H) demands the integration E2E 'per
environment' — six. This keeps ONE. §4-H wins on intent, N-6 on cost, and the narrowing is
recorded here as an explicit dated cut rather than left as a silent overrule.
⚠️ The Apple/Play guideline numbers are carried from 00-STAGE-3-14-RESEARCH.md and were NOT re-read
from developer.apple.com in this environment. COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH, cited with the word attached.
⚠️ ONE APP, STATED. e2e.yml is Subly-hardcoded and the brick stamps no integration_test/ at all, so
app #2 is born with no E2E and no harness to put one in. Generalising e2e.yml to a per-app matrix
is [9]R-1; stamping the E2E scaffold into the template is [3]S-2. This register describes the one
E2E that exists, and says so rather than implying a matrix.
⏱ 2026-09-25 · KEYED BY APP (O-E2E-LANE-WIRED-TO-ONE-APP). The one-app block that was `e2e` is now
`apps.<id>`, and each entry also names the tables the e2e purge deletes the throwaway user's rows
from (`userTables`) and the one table verify_row counts (`rowTable`). The databases are not here:
tooling/e2e/backend.mjs resolves them from E2E_APP_ID and services/<id>-api/wrangler.jsonc. `legs`
below are still the one app's six, so assert-e2e-legs.mjs reports COVERAGE LOST for a register that
names any number of apps other than one, until the legs are keyed by app too.
⏱ 2026-10-01 · THE LEGS ARE KEYED BY APP (rv2-newproduct-005, O-BRICK-STAMPS-NO-E2E-SUITE). The six legs moved from
the top level into each `apps.<id>.legs`, and assert-e2e-legs.mjs grades every entry against ITS OWN suite: an anchor
that stops resolving names the app (`apps/<id>`), and a blocker is re-evaluated over that app's own lib/ and suite. Every
app of the workspace set must have an entry; tooling/kit/stamp-shared.mjs writes a stamped app's entry with the brick
suite's legs (two asserted, four blocked), so app #2 is graded from its first commit instead of turning this guard
COVERAGE LOST. The sentences above that say "one app" are a dated measurement, left as written.
A stamped entry carries no userTables/rowTable: those name the tables the e2e purge deletes the throwaway user's rows
from, they belong to the app's backend, and tooling/e2e/backend.mjs refuses to purge until they are written.
`nativeTargets.app` names the app whose native suite and web legs limb NATIVE grades; the native axis is still one app's.

_targetAxis: APPENDED 2026-09-07 (ADR 067 · cutover-blockers). e2e.yml now carries an auth_target axis
(hosted | boxa), and `asserted` above is a HOSTED fact. Under auth_target=boxa the suite
returns early at apps/subscriptiontracker/integration_test/app_test.dart into expectOneIssuerRefusal, whose
own expectation is that the signed-in Home never loads its list — the anchors listed below
are still IN the file, which is what assert-e2e-legs greps for and why it still prints
'3 of 6 ... equality holds', but under boxa they are not REACHED. What a boxa run proves is
the one-issuer refusal (the deployed Worker rejects a Box A-minted session), not this leg.
Prose, deliberately: making the status target-shaped would need the guard to learn the axis,
and assert-e2e-legs.mjs is not this unit's file. Recorded so the first reader of a green
'asserted' after a boxa dispatch is not told the dashboard was reached.
⏱ 2026-09-25: the axis is no longer a target name. e2e.yml derives E2E_WORKERS_TRUST from the
run's SUPABASE_URL and tooling/platform-register.json vars.SUPABASE_URL, and `asserted` is a
fact of a run with trust `yes` (production, before and after the Phase 5 switch). A run with
trust `no` (a `selfhosted` dispatch before the switch) reads exactly as boxa did above.

⏱ 2026-09-26: and on a CAPTCHA-GATED stack (E2E_EXPECT_CAPTCHA_GATE=yes) the in-app half cannot delete:
the dialog's reauth is the Turnstile-gated password grant and a headless browser has no token (E2E live
run 36220597628). The suite then asserts the refusal ("Not deleted", reauthFailed, still signed in) and
tooling/e2e/delete_headless.mjs performs the erasure through the ungated /verify and the deployed
DELETE /v1/account; verify_purged.mjs audits it unchanged. The anchors below are the ungated walk's.
_why: PROMOTED 2026-08-08, and the excuse it replaced is the THIRD this leg has killed — which is the
design working three times. v1 'apps/subscriptiontracker has no delete-account call site' died when [ADR 027]
shipped the control. v2 'no deployed route erases apps/subscriptiontracker own database' died when
services/subscriptiontracker-api shipped DELETE /v1/account and the shared route began relaying to it. v3 'no
e2e step exercises the erasure route against the deployed API' dies here, because there is now a
step: integration_test/app_test.dart's third test signs in as a SECOND throwaway user, writes a
subscription through the live Worker, deletes the account from inside the running app, and lands
on the login screen — and tooling/e2e/verify_purged.mjs then re-reads live D1 and the GoTrue
admin API server-side.
🔴 THE ANCHORS BELOW COVER THE CLIENT HALF ONLY, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. They
resolve in the suite, which is all this guard can read. A client can only report what it was
told, so 'the app said Account deleted' is not 'the rows are gone' — the server-side half is
tooling/e2e/verify_purged.mjs, wired into e2e.yml between the D1 read-back and the teardown, and
it is held in place by assert-e2e-proof-fresh.mjs's REQUIRED_WORK rather than by this file.
Splitting the proof is deliberate; claiming the whole leg from four string matches would be the
overclaim N-6 already had.
⚠️ A SECOND THROWAWAY USER IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT TIDINESS. The delete walk destroys the account it
signs in with, and verify_row.mjs asserts COUNT(*) >= 1 for the FIRST user after the drive. One
user would mean leg 6 could only pass by turning leg 2 red.
⏱ 2026-09-29 · AB-E2E-02. READ BY tooling/ci/assert-e2e-legs.mjs limb NATIVE. Every leg above runs on web only, and
until today nothing graded a target axis at all: no leg ran on any native target and none declared an equivalent,
so a green nightly said nothing about android, ios, macos, windows or linux. The targets are NOT listed here as a
source: the guard derives them from tooling/channel-register.json (the platforms of every `surface: app` channel,
minus web), and a target with no row below for anonymous, sign-in AND account-delete-purges is COVERAGE LOST (exit 2).
`leg` means e2e.yml job `job` runs `drive` on that target on a declared schedule — the same drive
native-auth-proof.yml dispatches per auth change (tooling/e2e/native_auth_proof.mjs over each app's `suite`), which
walks first-run to the real sign-in form, signs in to Home and signs out. The guard refuses a `leg` whose job is
missing, does not list the target in its matrix, does not run the drive, or can only start on a cron the workflow
does not declare (a leg nothing runs). `legAnchors` must resolve in the comment-stripped suite, as the web anchors do.
`equivalent` means the leg is NOT walked on that target and names what proves it instead: `provenBy` must be a leg
the web suite has `asserted`, and `why` says why the web proof carries over. account-delete-purges is the one so
declared: the erasure is one Dart call (the chassis delete dialog -> DELETE /v1/account on the platform Worker) that
every target compiles from the same source, and the proof that matters is server-side — tooling/e2e/verify_purged.mjs
re-reading live D1 and the GoTrue admin API — which no target changes. Walking it natively would destroy the one
throwaway user each native leg signs in with.
⚠️ WEEKLY, NOT NIGHTLY, AND DATED: the native job runs on e2e.yml's Sunday cron. A cost choice, stated here, the same
way the web-only cut above was.
⏱ 2026-10-01 · train st-e2e-parity (EN-07): the native leg OPENS THE APP again (PROOF_NEEDS_DEVICE 'true'), and its
`sign-in` is the session reaching Home and signing out. Every target takes it from the harness token today (--sign-in
token), after the refusal probe proves the gate: a phone's form route needs an attestation no hosted device can produce
(ADR no.NNN), and a desktop's e-mail sign-in is the system-browser hand-off (#1133), which no app screen opens until that
work's PR B lands. Whether the FORM works is graded separately, by the `flows` row sign-in-form (web, today).
AB-O1-05. The list read back with the network off, on each target's own shared_preferences backend
(integration_test/offline_read_steps.dart). `anchors` resolve in the native suite, `webAnchors` in the web suite;
tooling/e2e/native_auth_proof.mjs requires the printed line of every run whose suite declares it.

why: One erasure call on every target (the chassis delete dialog -> DELETE /v1/account), and a server-side proof
(verify_purged.mjs) no target changes. The web leg walks it nightly; the native legs keep their user alive.

_why: READ BY tooling/ci/assert-captcha-gated-call-sites.mjs limb R3 (2026-09-26). Every captcha-gated call site
the suite above DRIVES — measured, not listed: the file uses an E2EKeys key the comment-stripped suite
uses — must appear here with two anchors. `refusal` resolves in the suite and is how it asserts the gate
refuses that surface on a gated stack. `headlessRoute` is how the leg still does its work there: a call
in the suite, or a tooling/e2e script the e2e workflow runs.
WHY: E2E live run 36220597628, the first run after the switch to Box C, failed its delete leg. The
dialog re-authenticates with the Turnstile-gated password grant, a headless browser has no token, and
GoTrue refused `captcha_failed` before any Worker was reached. Sign-in had been given /verify; the
delete dialog, driven by the same suite, had no route at all, and nothing could say so before the switch.
🔴 THE e2e LANE'S OWN THRESHOLD, read by tooling/e2e/assert-frames-carry-text.mjs and by nothing else.
It is deliberately NOT the store rule, storeMetadataContract.inkRule (tooling/channel-register.json), nor the per-frame inkFloor 0.7 that rule replaced on 2026-09-24.
That 0.7 means "a recapture of a recorded store frame may lose up to 30% of its ink" — a drift
allowance between two captures of the same frame. Reused here it meant "a frame's textless version
must be below 0.7 of itself", a different quantity, and it failed a correct frame on origin/main
🔴 A PER-FRAME SELF-RATIO DOES NOT SEPARATE AT e2e RESOLUTION — MEASURED 2026-09-23, not assumed.
Real frames of the live app, captured the way the drive captures (headless Chrome, 430x932, DPR 1),
once as served and once with every font request answered 200 text/html (the defect, reproduced):
page              served: measured textless ratio removed | glyphless: measured textless ratio removed
The glyphless RATIO spans 0.135-0.922, so a ratio test passes most of the defect: at DPR 1 the 9x9
mode filter also votes away hairlines, field underlines, checkbox outlines and icon strokes, and the
Turnstile iframe draws real HTML text even when Flutter draws none. Per frame, REMOVED ink
(measured - textless) separates only 1.33x (glyphless max 0.014331 vs served min 0.019022).
🔴 SO THE VERDICT IS ON THE RUN, WHICH IS THE UNIT THE DEFECT HAS. Fonts that did not arrive are
missing from every page at once. The MEDIAN of the run's removed ink is what is compared: glyphless
median 0.003698, served median 0.032481. The floor below is their geometric mean, rounded: the
glyphless median sits 2.97x under it, the served median 2.95x over it. The synthetic frame of
tooling/store/frame-ink.mjs (360x640) removes 0.022318 with glyphs (2.03x over) and 0.000078 without.
A median also holds when one page keeps its text (a Turnstile widget) or one page is text-light.
🔴 CALIBRATED AT ONE WIDTH. Removed ink is a fraction of pixels and falls roughly as 1/DPR (at 1129
wide, DPR 2.625, the served median is 0.015585 and the glyphless median 0.002887). A frame of any other
width is COVERAGE LOST (exit 2), never judged against a floor measured at a different size. A change
to --window-size in e2e.yml re-measures this block in the same change.
🔴 CORRECTED 2026-09-23, after the first nightly: the lever is --browser-dimension, not --window-size.
E2E live run 35824787614 read screenshots/00-consent.png as 1600x881. flutter drive resizes the window
to its own --browser-dimension default (1600x1024) over any --window-size, so every e2e frame since
c478ef35 (2026-07-18) was the desktop layout. The calibration frames here were 430x932 at DPR 1 by CDP
Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, which is what --browser-dimension=430x932@1 sets. e2e.yml passes
that now, and tooling/ci/test/assert-frames-carry-text.test.mjs holds its width and DPR to this block.
Evidence (frames, scripts, tables): Private/research/session-2026-09-23/frames-ink/. The served and
glyphless frames of five pages are committed as tooling/ci/test/fixtures/frames-ink-2026-09-23/.
framesCarryText.statistic: median over the run of (measured - textlessControl)

_why: ⏱ 2026-10-01 · train st-e2e-parity (EN-07, EN-08, XP-02). READ BY tooling/ci/assert-e2e-legs.mjs limb FLOWS. Feature
parity is locked: a flow ships only if it works on every target. The targets are DERIVED, as for nativeTargets, from
tooling/channel-register.json — every platform of a `surface: app` channel, web included — and every flow below must
name, for EACH, a `legs` entry (the suite that walks it — `web`: apps.<id>.test, `native`: nativeTargets.suite — and
anchors that resolve in that suite or an integration_test file it imports, comment-stripped) or an `equivalents`
entry (`provenBy`: a target where this flow is a leg, and a written `why`). A flow with neither on a target is a
finding (exit 1); an empty list is COVERAGE LOST (exit 2). Each leg asserts BEHAVIOUR — the server row, the prefs,
the feed, the file — through integration_test/flow_steps.dart, never presence.

list.asks: a reminder one minute out, tapped in the OS, lands on its /sub/<id>

why: The simulator has no host-side tap: simctl delivers a notification but nothing on a runner taps it without an
XCUITest harness. The tap -> payload -> /sub/<id> path is one Dart router (NotificationTapRouter) the Android leg walks.
Notification Center on a hosted macOS runner is not scriptable without an Accessibility grant the image does
not give. Same router as Android.
A toast is delivered only to the app's packaged identity (the MSIX), and a runner build is not one. Same router.
T5's scheduler shows through the desktop notification daemon, and xvfb runs none a host can click. Same router.
